newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Small-scale exporter and importer interest kept the rand in a tight band on Monday -- a trend which dealers said was expected to continue for the rest of the week.
After trading in a 4.6740 to 4.6800 bid range all day, the currency settled at 4.6765/6815 against the dollar compared with a 4.6800/6850 finish on Friday.
Dealers said the currency began the day under a little pressure from local banks looking to buy dollars as well as small amounts of month-end importer business.
However, the rand's rise to 4.68 was met by exporter selling which kept the currency in its range.
"It's been quiet all day...volumes have been pathetic," one trader said.
Dealers said the day's trend was expected to be extended through the whole week with most players still away on their Christmas holidays.
South African financial markets also close at 1000 GMT on Tuesday and are closed on Wednesday for the New Year's Day holiday.
On the bond market, yields were little changed after a moribund trading day.
"It has been desperately quiet with very thin volumes," one trader said, "and we are expecting it to remain quiet for the rest of the week. Life should come back into the market next Monday."
The key R150 settled at 16.085 percent from 16.14 percent on Friday.
On the money market three-month NCD rates were steady at 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at a year high of 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
The money market shortage stood at 11.117 billion rand on Saturday after rising to a record high of 11.126 billion rand on Friday.
Andre Kock, general manager of the Reserve Bank's money and capital market division, said the rise in the shortage had been expected because of the "strange" flow of notes in December.
"This is within estimates and the market should probably settle within the next week or two. One must expect these sort of movements in the short-term," Kock said.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners bought a net 12.70 million rand's worth of South African bonds last Tuesday after selling 25.38 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 424 million rand on Tuesday from 793.79 million rand on Monday.
